subproblem.title: Local mass is superadditive over finitely many pairwise disjoint regions
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and S an n-current in U (GeometricCurrentOn U n). Let ι be a type, s a finite subset of ι, and N : ι → Set(ℝ^P) with N_i ∩ N_j = ∅ for all distinct i, j ∈ s. Then Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_{⋃_{i∈s} N_i}(S) in [0, ∞]. Here M_W(S) = S.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(S ω) over test n-forms ω in U with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ι : Type) (s : Finset ι) (N : ι → Set (Euclid P)), (↑s : Set ι).PairwiseDisjoint N → ∑ i ∈ s, S.massOn (N i) ≤ S.massOn (⋃ i ∈ s, N i)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the supplied proof of cmcdtfr_boundary_variation, which glues near-optimal forms on the pairwise disjoint N_p. Here it is stated for an arbitrary current and an arbitrary finite disjoint family.

Notation. W := ⋃_{i∈s} N_i. For A ⊆ ℝ^P, Adm(A) := massAdmissibleOn U n A = {ω ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ω ⊆ A and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x}. M_A(S) := S.massOn A = sSup{ofReal(S ω) : ω ∈ Adm(A)}. Write |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Gluing. Let ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) for i ∈ s, and let ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i, a sum in the submodule TestFormOn U n. So ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and ω(x) = Σ_{i∈s} ω_i(x) (Submodule.coe_sum, Finset.sum_apply). We claim ω ∈ Adm(W) and S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i).
- (a) S is linear, so S(ω) = Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) (map_sum).
- (b) support ω ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} support ω_i (Finset.support_sum) ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i. The last set is closed (a finite union of closed sets) and contained in W. Hence tsupport ω = closure(support ω) ⊆ ⋃_{i∈s} tsupport ω_i ⊆ W (closure_minimal).
- (c) Fix x. If ω_i(x) = 0 for every i ∈ s, then ω(x) = 0 and |ω(x)| = 0 ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Otherwise choose i₀ ∈ s with ω_{i₀}(x) ≠ 0. Then x ∈ support ω_{i₀} ⊆ tsupport ω_{i₀} ⊆ N_{i₀}. For i ∈ s with i ≠ i₀, N_i ∩ N_{i₀} = ∅ gives x ∉ N_i ⊇ tsupport ω_i, so ω_i(x) = 0. Hence ω(x) = ω_{i₀}(x) (Finset.sum_eq_single) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1.
2. Monotonicity. For i ∈ s, N_i ⊆ W, so M_{N_i}(S) ≤ M_W(S) (massOn_mono).
3. Reduction. If M_W(S) = ∞, the claim is trivial. Assume M_W(S) < ∞ from now on. By step 2 each M_{N_i}(S), i ∈ s, is finite. Put V_i := M_{N_i}(S).toReal ≥ 0, so that ofReal(V_i) = M_{N_i}(S) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
4. Near-optimal forms. Let η > 0. For each i ∈ s choose ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) with S(ω_i) ≥ V_i − η, as follows.
- If V_i ≤ η, take ω_i := 0. It lies in Adm(N_i), since tsupport 0 = ∅ and |0| = 0, and S(0) = 0 ≥ V_i − η.
- If V_i > η, then ofReal(V_i − η) < ofReal(V_i) = M_{N_i}(S). By lt_sSup_iff some ω_i ∈ Adm(N_i) satisfies ofReal(V_i − η) < ofReal(S(ω_i)). Since ofReal is monotone, this forces V_i − η < S(ω_i).
5. Glue. By step 1, ω := Σ_{i∈s} ω_i ∈ Adm(W). So ofReal(S ω) ≤ M_W(S) (le_massOn), and therefore S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal, M_W(S) ≠ ∞). With step 4: Σ_{i∈s} V_i − |s|·η = Σ_{i∈s}(V_i − η) ≤ Σ_{i∈s} S(ω_i) = S(ω) ≤ M_W(S).toReal.
6. Limit. For s = ∅ the sum is 0. Otherwise apply step 5 with η := ε/|s| for each ε > 0, getting Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal + ε. By le_of_forall_pos_le_add, Σ_{i∈s} V_i ≤ M_W(S).toReal.
7. Conclusion. Σ_{i∈s} M_{N_i}(S) = Σ_{i∈s} ofReal(V_i) = ofReal(Σ_{i∈s} V_i) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, V_i ≥ 0) ≤ ofReal(M_W(S).toReal) = M_W(S), by monotonicity of ofReal and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: Forms ω_i admissible for the pairwise disjoint N_i have at most one nonzero value at each point. So Σ ω_i is admissible for ⋃ N_i, and S(Σ ω_i) = Σ S(ω_i).
If M_{⋃N}(S) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise every M_{N_i}(S) is finite.
Choose ω_i with S(ω_i) ≥ M_{N_i}(S).toReal − η and glue them: Σ_i M_{N_i}(S).toReal − |s|η ≤ M_{⋃N}(S).toReal.
Let η → 0 and convert back to [0, ∞] with ofReal.

audit.reason: The contract correctly permits arbitrary pairwise disjoint regions. Finite support gluing preserves admissibility because at most one summand is nonzero at each point. The proof handles infinite mass, zero local masses, the empty family, supremum approximation, and finite-mass ENNReal conversions without additional hypotheses.
